issue.description:
Found 2026-08-20 while installing plan-review 2.0. The in-progress lib extraction (uncommitted WIP in plan-author/plan-review/readme-review/spec-review scripts, untracked lib/common.sh) has each script do: source "$(dirname "$0")/../../lib/common.sh". Correct inside the repo, but once a skill is installed to ~/.claude/skills/<skill>/ that path resolves to ~/.claude/lib/common.sh. install.sh copies only the skill directory, so every refactored script fails at its source line with 'No such file or directory' (verified: installed plan-review/scripts/scan-headers.sh exits 1). The parent bead's own spec prescribes that exact path, so the defect is in the spec, not just the WIP.

Options: (a) install.sh also installs lib/ to ~/.claude/skills/lib/ — only works if repo skills and installed skills share the same relative layout; (b) guard the source with an inline fallback — defeats most of the dedup; (c) inline lib/common.sh into each script at install time (a tiny build step in install.sh) — repo stays DRY, installed copies stay self-contained. Recommended: (c). Acceptance: plan-review's SELF-TEST fixture and scan-headers.sh run green from the INSTALLED path, and scripts/check-installed.sh reports no drift.

Until fixed, the installed plan-review carries the HEAD (self-contained) scan-headers.sh and score-plan.sh, so check-installed.sh reports drift on those two files by design.

Dormant at HEAD (lib/ absent, inline_lib_common early-returns; repo scripts are +x and self-contained).

issue.notes:
Requested by the operator on 2026-09-21: "statusline updated to include the host machine as cpu usage / cpu total (cpu %) and ram usage / ram total (ram %)". They believed it had been added some time ago. It had not, anywhere: not in the live ~/.claude/usage-statusline.sh, not in ~/.claude/skills/usage-statusline, not in this repo, and no commit in this repo or claude-config ever introduced /proc/loadavg or MemTotal. The earlier ask survives only in shell history ("statusline to show cpu usage (load / total cores) and ramp usage (Used / total (%))") — it was dropped without landing.

ADDED — two segments before the commit counter, same 50/80 colour thresholds as the quota windows so one glance reads the whole line the same way:

  5h 20% ██▒▒░░░░░░ ~9h │ 7d 79% ███████░░░ ~35h │ Fable 94% ███████▓▓░ ~8h │ cpu 3.9/20 19% │ ram 25/62G 41% │ ⎇ 2656

  cpu = 1-minute loadavg / core count, with load/cores as the percentage.
  ram = (MemTotal - MemAvailable) / MemTotal in GiB, with the percentage.

DECISIONS WORTH KEEPING:

1. Read /proc directly, no top/free/vmstat. This renders on every prompt, so it
   is pure bash string work plus a single nproc.

2. MemAvailable, NOT MemFree. MemFree excludes reclaimable page cache and would
   have reported this box as ~95% used while 36G was actually available.
   Cross-checked against `free -g` at write time: script said 25/62G, free said
   total 62 used 25 available 36.

3. Assignment form x=$(( ... )) everywhere, never bare (( ... )). The script runs
   under `set -euo pipefail`, and a bare arithmetic command evaluating to zero
   returns exit status 1 — so the statusline would have blanked itself the moment
   load rounded down to 0%. Verified: load 0.00 renders "0.0/20 0%" and the
   script exits 0.

4. 10# prefix on the fractional part. /proc/loadavg gives two decimals, so a load
   of 0.04 yields the substring "04", which bash arithmetic reads as octal.
   Verified 0.04 -> 0%.

5. Overload is rendered, not clamped: load 41.20 on 20 cores prints 206%, load
   100.00 prints 500%. This box sat at load 21+ (normalized 1.08) earlier the
   same day while NEEDLE refused worker launches for CPU saturation, which is
   exactly the condition the segment exists to make visible. Clamping at 100%
   would hide the difference between "busy" and "wedged".

6. host_ok gates both segments, so an unreadable /proc (container, kernel change)
   drops them rather than blanking the line.

makes it durable — the other two are machine-local and a re-install from this

issue.description:
9 skills each carry their own scripts/score-*.sh or scan-*.sh (release-readiness/scripts/scan-release.sh,
repo-hygiene/scripts/repo_hygiene.sh, plan-review/scripts/scan-headers.sh + score-plan.sh,
spec-review/scripts/score-spec.sh, diff-review/scripts/collect-diff.sh,
plan-author/scripts/score-draft.sh, api-design-review/scripts/scan-api.sh,
test-plan-review/scripts/scan-tests.sh, readme-review/scripts/score-readme.sh). Each
independently reimplements: markdown frontmatter parsing, markdown section/header scanning,
and percent/color terminal output formatting.

Add a shared lib/common.sh at repo root with the deduplicated versions of these three
utilities, and refactor the 9 scripts above to source it (`source
"$(dirname "$0")/../../lib/common.sh"` or equivalent relative path) instead of reimplementing.
Keep each script's actual scoring logic (the part specific to that skill) untouched — this is
a pure extraction, not a behavior change. Run each refactored script against its existing
sample/fixture input (where one exists, e.g. plan-review's SELF-TEST.md sample) before/after
to confirm output is byte-identical.

issue.notes:
Found via the new SELF-TEST.md fixtures (jedscura-60651fb7, commit 63de232): the in-flight lib/common.sh check() DROPPED a guard that HEAD's inline score-readme.sh had. HEAD line 49: grep -qiE -e "$pattern" — the lib version is grep -qiE "$pattern". Consequence: score-readme check 2.7 passes the literal pattern '--version', which grep parses as its --version FLAG — grep's version banner prints into every score-readme run and the check 'passes' without reading the file. This bead's own bar is byte-identical before/after; restore -e (or --) in check() or that bar fails for readme-review. Also relevant to the byte-identical check: print_failures() plus the scripts' unconditional trailing echo emits one extra blank line where HEAD printed none when FAILURES is empty (visible in spec-review/score-spec.sh with an all-passing fixture) — cosmetic, but it will show up in a byte diff. The six new SELF-TEST.md files are the before/after fixtures to run per script: spec-review, plan-author, readme-review, api-design-review, test-plan-review, release-readiness — each pins exact expected output; readme-review's pins are built to hold with or without the -e fix (fixture passes 2.7 legitimately via 'You should see').

issue.description:
Incident 2026-09-23: the statusline went completely blank. The usage API began returning a third limit (weekly_scoped, Fable) whose resets_at is "2026-09-30T01:00:00+00:00" — no fractional seconds, unlike the other limits ("...59.726900+00:00"). The jq `ts` helper only rewrote ".<digits>+00:00" to "Z", so fromdateiso8601 rejected the string and jq aborted mid-output. `eval "$(jq ... 2>/dev/null)"` swallowed the error, the scoped-limit variables (p7f...) were never set, and `set -euo pipefail` killed the script at the first use ("p7f: unbound variable", exit 1). The harness renders nothing on a non-zero exit.

Immediate fix (already applied live to ~/.claude/usage-statusline.sh, NOT yet in this repo): make the fractional part optional in `ts`.

SCOPE of this bead — harden usage-statusline/scripts/usage-statusline.sh so future API/format changes degrade one segment instead of blanking the line:
- Parse the usage JSON defensively: tolerate missing/null/float/string percent, missing or differently formatted resets_at (any fraction, any UTC offset, epoch seconds/ms), missing limit kinds, multiple weekly_scoped limits.
- Quote everything eval'd from jq (@sh); display_name with spaces or metacharacters must not break or inject into eval.
- Isolate each rendered segment so a failure in one cannot kill the rest; always exit 0.
- Host (cpu/ram) and commit segments render even when quota data is unavailable.
- Cache: validate before writing, write atomically (temp + mv), tolerate a corrupt/empty cache.
- Fetch must not block rendering or retry every render on failure; background it with stdio detached.
- Credential refresh must never write a malformed token set (validate the response) and never leave the file world-readable (umask 077).
- Failures are logged to the cache dir so the next diagnosis does not need a repro; a stale cache is visibly marked.
- Add a fixture-based regression test covering the incident shape and the drift cases above.
- Update SKILL.md / README.md / SELF-TEST.md where behaviour they describe changes (e.g. "blank output until first fetch").

OUT OF SCOPE: changing what the quota windows mean, the API endpoints, or the token-refresh protocol itself.

Deployment: canonical source is this repo; deploy with ./install.sh usage-statusline, verify with scripts/check-installed.sh usage-statusline.

The live one-line hotfix had been applied to ~/.claude/usage-statusline.sh only; this change supersedes it.

DECISIONS
1. Dropped set -euo pipefail (reverses decision 3 of jedscura-a74db3d7; its x=$(( )) assignment form is kept and still harmless). Each segment renders in a subshell instead, because bash aborts the whole command list on an arithmetic error (probed). Always exit 0.
2. No eval. jq emits US-delimited records, `read` splits them. The old eval really executed $(...) in a display_name (reproduced: created a file).
3. Missing/unreadable quota data => `usage n/a` with cpu/ram/git still shown. This DELIBERATELY reverses the old pinned "first run is blank" behaviour (SELF-TEST case 1).
4. Multiple weekly_scoped limits => show the highest percent (was: last one, by accident of jq generator semantics). Unknown kinds ignored. Legacy five_hour/seven_day/seven_day_{opus,sonnet} used if `limits` disappears.
5. Fetch is detached (stdout/stdin closed) and rate-limited to 1 attempt/60s via usage.attempt; previously it blocked rendering up to 8s per prompt when the API was slow, and retried on every render while failing.
6. Cache written atomically after a shape check; a rejected 200 is kept in usage.rejected.json and the last good cache keeps serving (marked `stale <age>` after 15 min).
7. Credentials (found by the new suite, not by the incident): old refresh rewrote .credentials.json at mode 644, wrote null tokens if a 200 had an unexpected body, and put both tokens on curl's argv. Now: umask 077, response validated, compare-and-swap on the refresh token, tokens via stdin/env only. Refresh PROTOCOL itself (endpoint, camelCase body) deliberately unchanged, per this bead's out-of-scope.
8. Regression tests live in SELF-TEST.md (repo convention) and are NOT wired into test-script-fixtures.sh / pre-commit: that suite explicitly scopes usage-statusline out, and CI's skills-validate image may lack jq/flock. Wiring it is a separate, deliberate call.

issue.description:
Define the exact contract for scripts/install-review-timers.sh before implementation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Specify the three workspace review service/timer names, the separate memory-tool unit names, and which generated files are owned by the installer.
- Specify the weekly stagger, workspace-list input, PATH requirement, Type=oneshot, timeout, Nice=10, and systemd user scope.
- Specify idempotent reinstall and --uninstall behavior that removes only installer-owned files.
- Record the contract in the bead notes or an implementation-facing repository document without changing unrelated files.
issue.notes:
Contract for scripts/install-review-timers.sh (definition only; no source-file change required because the checked-in README and fixture already describe this surface):

Required systemd --user review pairs:
- Workspace review: factory-review-plan-vs-built.service and factory-review-plan-vs-built.timer; weekly Monday at 02:00 local time; runs the plan-vs-built review over every configured workspace.
- Workspace review: factory-review-find-stubs.service and factory-review-find-stubs.timer; weekly Tuesday at 02:00 local time; runs the find-stubs review over every configured workspace.
- Workspace review: factory-review-repo-hygiene.service and factory-review-repo-hygiene.timer; weekly Wednesday at 02:00 local time; runs the repo-hygiene review over every configured workspace.
- Separate host check: factory-review-memory-tool.service and factory-review-memory-tool.timer; weekly Thursday at 02:00 local time; runs once per timer invocation and does not read the workspace list.

The current installer also has one explicitly auxiliary, machine-local pair: factory-review-installed-drift.service and factory-review-installed-drift.timer, Friday at 02:00. It is not a fourth workspace review and is outside the required three-workspace plus memory-tool surface, but it is included in the installer-owned artifact set.

Workspace-list input is $HOME/.config/factory-review/workspaces.txt, one workspace path per line. Blank lines and comment lines are ignored; ~ and non-absolute entries resolve from $HOME. The three workspace runners consume this file; the memory-tool and auxiliary installed-drift runners ignore it. A missing list is initialized with comments by install and yields no workspace reviews until populated.

Generated artifacts owned by the installer are, for each declared unit above:
- $HOME/.config/systemd/user/<unit>.service
- $HOME/.config/systemd/user/<unit>.timer
- $HOME/.config/factory-review/<unit>.sh
The generated workspace list is user input/configuration, not an uninstall-owned artifact: install may create it when absent, but --uninstall preserves it. Same-named files without the installer ownership marker are foreign; install refuses to overwrite them and uninstall leaves them byte-for-byte unchanged. Marker-owned stale unit artifacts from an older declared set may be reconciled/removed.

Every generated service is systemd user scope, Type=oneshot, TimeoutSec=30min, Nice=10, with journal stdout/stderr. The service baseline PATH is /run/current-system/sw/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin. Generated runners extend PATH so user-installed commands are available: workspace runners use /run/current-system/sw/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH, and memory-tool uses $HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH. The installer resolves bash with command -v and embeds that executable path. Timers use Persistent=true and the local user manager via systemctl --user.

Reinstall is idempotent: it regenerates the same owned files, does not create duplicate units, reloads the user manager, and re-enables the owned timers; it refuses foreign collisions. --uninstall stops/disables only an installer-owned timer when a user manager is available, removes only marker-owned service/timer/runner files, reloads the user manager, and preserves workspaces.txt plus all foreign files and units.
